issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's own conventions (Phi_t = Phi_{0,t} is the forward flow, Phi = Phi_{0,1}, and mu = Phi_*nu), change of variables plus Liouville's formula give log f_{Phi_*nu}(y) = log f_nu(Phi^{-1}(y)) - ∫_0^1 div v(Phi_t(Phi^{-1}(y)),t) dt: the divergence integral enters with a MINUS sign and along the trajectory ending at y (started at Phi^{-1}(y)). The printed identity has a plus sign and integrates along the forward trajectory started at y. Concrete counterexample: d=1, v(x,t)=ax with a>0. Then Phi(z)=e^a z and f_{Phi_*nu}(y) = e^{-a} f_nu(e^{-a} y), so the true log-density is log f_nu(e^{-a}y) - a, whereas the printed formula yields log f_nu(e^{-a}y) + ∫_0^1 a dt = log f_nu(e^{-a}y) + a.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the display by log f_{Phi_*nu}(y) = log f_nu(Phi^{-1}(y)) - ∫_0^1 div v(Phi_t(Phi^{-1}(y)),t) dt (the standard FFJORD form), and correct the adjacent sampling sentence (samples from Phi_*nu are Phi(z), obtained by solving the ODE forward).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed identity motivating the likelihood objective (neural_ode_log_likelihood) is false as written; evaluated as printed it miscomputes the model log-density by a sign-flipped log-Jacobian along the wrong trajectory. No subsequent proof uses the identity (the analysis in Theorem thm:learnability_target_class and Lemma lem:sub_gaussian uses change of variables with |det D Phi^{-1}| directly), so all formal results are unaffected; only the training-formula discussion in Section 2.3 is wrong.
issues.title: Liouville log-density identity has wrong sign and wrong flow argument
issues.why_classification: A forced one-line correction to a displayed identity that is never invoked in any proof; every theorem, constant, and guarantee survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The generalization error is defined with a supremum over |Z_{theta,n}|, and McDiarmid is later applied to f = sup_theta |f_theta|, but the first equality of the proof identifies E[eps^gen] with E[sup_theta Z_{theta,n}], dropping the absolute value. Since the centered process takes negative values, sup|Z| >= sup Z with strict inequality in general, so the equality is false. Bounding E sup|Z| through Dudley's entropy integral requires applying it to both Z and -Z (the sub-Gaussian bound is symmetric), which costs an additional factor 2. The derivable conclusion is therefore E[eps^gen] <= 96 q bar L / sqrt(n), not the stated 48 L W^2 bar L / sqrt(n).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Dudley's integral to Z and to -Z (or use E sup|Z| <= E sup Z + E sup(-Z)) and restate the bound with the doubled constant (96 q bar L/sqrt(n)), propagating the adjusted constant through thm:concentration_bound and the main theorem's thresholds.
issues.overall_effect: The constant 48 in the statement of thm:dudley is not established; thm:concentration_bound, whose centering term 48 L W^2 bar L/sqrt(n) is justified only via Theorem thm:dudley, inherits the unsupported constant, as do the threshold calibrations in the proof of thm:learnability_sparse_grid.
issues.title: Dudley bound drops the absolute value in the generalization error
issues.why_classification: Only constant factors change; every convergence statement, threshold existence claim, and the final PAC guarantee survive with the adjusted constants, and the repair is a standard one-line symmetrization.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives E[eps^gen] <= 48 q bar L / sqrt(n) and then invokes q <= 2LW^2 to 'complete the proof' of the stated bound 48 L W^2 bar L / sqrt(n). But q <= 2LW^2 yields only 48 q <= 96 L W^2, so the stated constant is too small by a factor 2; the inference 48q <= 48LW^2 is invalid. For the architecture (d+1, W, ..., W, d) the exact count is q = (L-1)W(W+1) + 2(d+1)W + d, which exceeds LW^2 in regimes such as L > W - 2d - 1 (e.g., L=10, W=3, d=2 gives q=128 > 90 = LW^2), so the statement is not even rescued by q <= LW^2 in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem with constant 96 L W^2 (or with 48 q) in place of 48 L W^2 and propagate the adjusted constant through thm:concentration_bound and the thresholds in the main theorem.
issues.overall_effect: Independently of the absolute-value slip, the constant in thm:dudley's statement is unsupported; the centering constant in thm:concentration_bound, which quotes the 48 L W^2 bar L/sqrt(n) bound, is likewise unsupported and must be enlarged.
issues.title: Final step of Dudley bound mis-infers the 48LW^2 constant from q <= 2LW^2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a forced constant change with no loss of mathematical content, no change to the method, and no effect on any convergence or PAC conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The quadrature error is controlled by (eq:main_thm_sg_error_bd), whose left-hand side carries the prefactor (1 + sqrt(d) e^{sqrt(d) sqrt(q) Lip_1^Theta}) evaluated at the growing architecture (L_n, W_n). Since L_n, W_n -> infinity and Lip_1^Theta(L_n,W_n,d) -> infinity (rmk:lip_const_bound), this prefactor diverges as n -> infinity, so the threshold m(n) that makes the quadrature term <= eps/2 necessarily grows with n. The proof therefore only establishes the PAC bound for pairs (n, m) with m >= m(n), an n-dependent threshold. The theorem (and the PAC definition (defn:pac_learnability) it claims to instantiate) asserts a single fixed threshold m(eps,delta) := m(n(eps,delta)) that works simultaneously for ALL n >= n(eps,delta); for fixed m and n -> infinity the prefactor keeps growing, so (eq:main_thm_sg_error_bd) eventually fails and the final inference is invalid. No argument in the source controls ||Phi^{hat theta_n}||_{C^1} uniformly in n (e.g., via a complexity-penalized ERM), so the uniform-in-n quadrature control needed for the stated guarantee is missing.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem (and instantiate the PAC notion accordingly) as: for all n >= n(eps,delta) and all m >= m(n,eps,delta); the existing proof then goes through verbatim. Recovering the stated independent-threshold version would require a genuinely new ingredient, such as complexity regularization of the ERM to bound ||Phi^{hat theta_n}||_{C^1} uniformly in n.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's main result is established only with the number of quadrature points adapted to the sample size (m >= m(n,eps,delta), with m(n,eps,delta) -> infinity). The advertised guarantee with independent thresholds - any m above a fixed threshold, simultaneously for all large n, as formalized in (defn:pac_learnability) - is unproven, so the conclusion 'PAC-learnable in the sense of (defn:pac_learnability)' does not follow as stated; the abstract-level consistency claim survives only in the coupled form.
issues.title: Quadrature-point threshold must grow with n; the stated independent-threshold PAC guarantee is not established
issues.why_classification: The supported resolution is a contained quantifier weakening: no new proof architecture is needed, no rate is lost (no rates are stated), and a recognizably comparable PAC-consistency result (adaptive network capacity with adaptive quadrature resolution, matching the abstract) survives; but the formal guarantee changes from independent to coupled thresholds, which is more than a local or constant-level repair.

issues.failure_explanation: The decomposition established in the paper is KL(mu || mu_{hat theta_n}) <= eps^model + 2 eps^gen (empirical_error_decomp), but the main proof invokes it as KL <= eps^model + eps^gen (main_thm_emp_error_decomp), silently dropping the factor 2. The subsequent probability chain is calibrated to the wrong decomposition: from eps^model + 2 eps^gen > eps^2/(8||qoi||^2) and eps^model <= eps^2/(16||qoi||^2) one only gets eps^gen > eps^2/(32||qoi||^2), not the eps^2/(16||qoi||^2) used; the expectation shift (eq:main_thm_exp_gen_err_bd) and the final exponent constant 4096 are correspondingly miscalibrated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reinstate the factor 2 from (empirical_error_decomp) and recalibrate the thresholds: e.g., require eps^model <= eps^2/(32||qoi||^2), control eps^gen at level eps^2/(32||qoi||^2) with expectation bound <= eps^2/(64||qoi||^2), and enlarge the final constant accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Internal constants of the main theorem's proof are wrong (thresholds 16 -> 32, 32 -> 64, and the final exponent constant 4096 must be enlarged). The theorem statement is unaffected once the constants are recalibrated.
issues.title: Main proof drops the factor 2 in the empirical error decomposition
issues.why_classification: The correction is a forced constant adjustment; no inference structure, guarantee, rate, or scope changes, and all conclusions survive verbatim with the corrected constants.
